chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Suleiman! Do you know who is the Muslim?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! You are more knowing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Muslim is the one from whom the Muslims are safe from his tongue and his hand.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And do you know who is the believer?' I said, 'You are more knowing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the believer is the one upon whom the Muslims trust with their wealth and their selves; and the Muslim is prohibited upon the Muslim that he is unjust to him, or abandons him, or drives him away with intransigence.'
ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of a Muslim and a believer according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between the general safety of the 'Muslim' (salvation from harm) and the deeper trustworthiness of the 'Mu'min' (reliability in wealth and self), a distinction central to Shia jurisprudence regarding social contracts. The narration further codifies the rights of Muslims over one another, prohibiting oppression, abandonment, or aggressive dismissal, thereby establishing the ethical baseline for communal harmony.
